tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

Reference for writing any document an agent consumes: a skill, an `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, a doc reached by a pointer. The packaging differs; the writing does not: the same levers make each one predictable, since the agent takes the same _process_ every run rather than producing the same output.

When the document you're writing is a skill, read [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md) for frontmatter, invocation choice, and router skills.

## Context pointers

A **context pointer** is a reference held in the agent's context that names some out-of-context material and encodes the condition for reaching it. A skill's description is one; a line in `AGENTS.md` naming a doc is the same object. The pointer's _wording_, not its target, decides when the agent reaches the material, and how reliably. A must-have target behind a weakly worded pointer is a variance bug: sharpen the wording first, and inline the material only if sharpening fails.

A pointer does two jobs: state what the material is, and list the **branches** that should trigger reaching it (a branch is a distinct case the document handles, so different runs take different paths through it). Every word of an always-loaded pointer costs on every turn, so it earns even harder pruning than the body:

- **Front-load the leading word**: the pointer is where it does its triggering work.
- **One trigger per branch.** Synonyms that rename a single branch are one branch written twice; collapse them and keep only genuinely distinct branches.
- **Cut identity the body already carries.**

## The two loads

Every document and pointer you add spends one of two budgets:

- **Context load** is the cost of always-loaded material on the agent's window: an `AGENTS.md` line, a skill description, anything sitting in context every turn, spending tokens and attention whether or not it fires.
- **Cognitive load** is the cost on the human: which documents exist and when to reach for each. The human is the index. Not a cost to minimise: it is the price of human agency; spend it where human judgement matters, remove it where it does not.

Material reached only through a pointer escapes context load at the price of the pointer's own line; material with no pointer at all rides entirely on cognitive load.

## Information hierarchy

A document is built from two content types: **steps** (the ordered actions the agent performs) and **reference** (definitions, rules, facts consulted on demand). The two mix freely: all steps (a recipe), all reference (a review's rules, this skill), or both. The core decision is where each piece sits on the **information hierarchy**, a ladder ranked by how immediately the agent needs the material:

1. **In-file step** is the primary tier: what the agent does, in order.
2. **In-file reference** is consulted on demand. Often a legitimately flat peer-set (every rule of a review on one rung), which is a fine arrangement, not a smell.
3. **Disclosed reference** is pushed out into a separate file, reached by a context pointer, loaded only when the pointer fires. Spans a sibling file in the same folder through fully external reference that lives anywhere and any document can point at.

Push too little down and the top bloats; push too much and you hide material the agent actually needs. That tension is the whole decision.

**Progressive disclosure** is the move down the ladder (out of the main file and behind a pointer) so the top stays legible. Not primarily a token optimisation: it is how the hierarchy is protected. Branching is the cleanest disclosure test: inline what every branch needs, and push behind a pointer what only some branches reach. When a document has steps, in-file reference that should be disclosed buries them and turns attending to them into a coin-flip: a variance lever, not just a legibility one.

**Co-location** is the within-file companion: where the ladder decides _how far down_ a piece sits, co-location decides _what sits beside it_ once there. Keep a concept's definition, rules, and caveats under one heading rather than scattered, so reading one part brings its neighbours with it. The test: the document should read like documentation written for the agent. Grouped material reads that way; scattered material does not. (Distinct from duplication: that repeats one meaning in two places; scattering fragments one meaning across many.)

**Sprawl** is the failure mode here: a document simply too long, even when every line is live and unique. Attention thins across the excess, and every extra line is one more to keep relevant. The cure is the ladder: disclose reference behind pointers, and split by branch or sequence so each path carries only what it needs.

## Steps and completion criteria

Every step ends on a **completion criterion**, the condition that tells the agent the work is done. Two properties make it a lever:

- **Clarity**: can the agent tell done from not-done? A vague bound ("understanding reached") invites **premature completion**: ending the step before it is genuinely done, attention slipping to _being done_. The visible steps still ahead (the **post-completion steps**) supply the pull; the criterion's clarity is the resistance. Defend in order: **sharpen the bound first** (local and cheap); only if it is irreducibly fuzzy _and_ you observe the rush, hide the later steps by splitting the sequence. Hiding only works across a real context boundary (a hand-off or a subagent dispatch; an inline call leaves the later steps in context and clears nothing).
- **Demand**: how much it requires. "Every modified model accounted for" forces thorough work where "produce a change list" does not. Demand drives **legwork** (the digging the agent does within the work, latent in the wording rather than written as its own step), and it is not step-bound: "every rule applied" binds a body of flat reference just as "every step done" binds a sequence, which is how an all-reference document still carries an exhaustiveness bar.

The strongest criteria are both checkable and exhaustive.

## When to split

Splitting one document into two spends one of the two loads, so split only when the cut earns it:

- **By sequence**: split a run of steps where the post-completion steps tempt the agent to rush the one in front of it. Keeping them out of view drives more legwork on the current task. Beware the reverse: merging sequences exposes each step's later steps to what follows, inviting premature completion.
- **By invocation**, skill-specific: see [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md).

## Leading words

A **leading word** is a compact concept already living in the model's pretraining that the agent thinks with while running the document (_lesson_, _fog of war_, _tracer bullets_). Repeated as a token, never as a sentence, it accumulates a distributed definition and anchors a whole region of behaviour in the fewest tokens, by recruiting priors the model already holds. Coining your own works if you define it clearly, but a made-up word recruits no priors: you pay in definition tokens what a pretrained word gives free; reach for an existing word first.

It anchors twice. In the body, _execution_: the agent reaches for the same behaviour every time the word appears, and inside flat reference it focuses attention on a class of thing to look for. In a pointer, _invocation_: when the same word lives in your prompts, your docs, and your codebase, the agent links that shared language to the material and reaches it more reliably.

Hunt for opportunities to refactor with leading words. A triad spelled out at three sites, a pointer spending a sentence to gesture at one idea. Each is a passage begging to collapse into a single token:

- "fast, deterministic, low-overhead" → _tight_ (a _tight_ loop).
- "a loop you believe in" → _red_, turning a fuzzy gate into a binary observable state (the loop goes _red_ on the bug, or it doesn't).

You win twice: fewer tokens, and a sharper hook for the agent to hang its thinking on. Assume every document is carrying restatements that leading words retire. Go find them.

**Negation** is the failure mode beside this lever: steering by prohibition drags the forbidden behaviour into context and makes it _more_ available, not less. _Don't think of an elephant_, and the elephant is all there is; the negation is a weak modifier the strongly-activated concept overruns, so the ban half-reads as an instruction to do the thing. Prompt the **positive**: state the target behaviour ("write one-line comments") so the banned one is never spoken. A prohibition earns its place only as a hard guardrail you cannot phrase positively; even then, pair it with the positive target so attention lands on what to do.

## Pruning

- Keep each meaning in a **single source of truth**: one authoritative place, so changing the behaviour is a one-place edit. **Duplication** (the same meaning in more than one place) costs maintenance and tokens, and inflates a meaning's prominence on the ladder past its real rank. (The accidental inverse of a leading word, which repeats a token on purpose, never the meaning.)
- The **environment** is a source of truth too (`package.json` scripts, config files, the directory layout, `--help` output), and a document that restates it is a **cache**: a copy of a lookup, earning its load only when the lookup is expensive. Cache what the agent cannot find by looking: the unwritten convention, the reason behind a choice, the gotcha no config confesses. Leave the one-file, one-command lookups to the environment, where they cannot go stale.
- Check every line for **relevance**: does it still bear on what the document does? A line loses relevance by never bearing on the task (mere exposition, or a branch that should be disclosed) or by going stale as the behaviour or world it describes changes. Shorter documents are easier to keep relevant. Without a pruning discipline the default fate is **sediment**: stale layers that settle because adding feels safe and removing feels risky, until you must core down through them to find what is still live.
- Hunt **no-ops** sentence by sentence: an instruction the model already obeys by default pays load to say nothing. The test (does it change behaviour versus the default?) is model-relative, not reader-relative: two people disagreeing about a no-op disagree about the default, and settle it by running the document, not by debate. When a sentence fails, delete the whole sentence rather than trim words from it. The test also grades leading words: a word too weak to beat the default (_be thorough_ when the agent is already thorough-ish) is a no-op, and the fix is a stronger word (_relentless_), not a different technique.

---
name: project
description: >-
  Manage the portfolio project registry (ideas, updates, ranking, promotion, dev stages,
  start/park/done, receivers) and open the live project board. Use when the user says
  "/project", "new idea:", "log progress on", "project update", "add to my project
  inbox", "show my projects", "re-rank my projects", "set the stage on", "mark <project>
  as spec'd/planned/shipped", "start/park <project>". Do not use for the DEV drift
  dashboard (use project-triage) or to scaffold a new repo (use new-project).
---

# /project — portfolio registry skill

Drives the `project-triage` CLI to capture ideas, log progress and change
project status. The registry (`portfolio.json`) is the single source of truth.
The live board (`board.py`) is its front door and re-renders on its own within
a few seconds of any registry change, so there is nothing to render or publish.
(The static `dashboard.html`, its Artifact and `pulse.md` retired 2026-10-03.)

## Paths

- Config: `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.windows.json` on Windows; `config.macos.json` on macOS
- Repo: parent directory of `portfolio_json` in the selected platform config
- Interpreter: `python` on Windows; `python3` on macOS
- Registry: `portfolio_json` in the selected platform config
- CLI entry points: `portfolio.py` (mutations and checks), `board.py` (the board)

## CLI contract (verbatim — do not alter flags)

```
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<source>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" add-update "<name>" "<note>" --next-action "<optional>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" set-status "<name>" active|paused|done --note "<optional>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" set-receiver "<name>" "<who, or me: why>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" slate-check
python "<project-triage-repo>/board.py" --background
```

- `add-idea` prints `idea captured (<N> in inbox)`.
- `add-update` prints `updated <name>` (name match is case-insensitive).
- `set-stage` prints `stage set: <name> → <stage>`. Valid stages, in ladder
  order: `idea grilled spec planned building shipped`.
- `set-status` prints `status set: <name> → <status>`. It is the board's
  Start/Park/Done: a start over the slate cap is refused, and a start begins
  the 7-day clock.
- `slate-check` loads (and so validates) the registry and prints the slate
  rules; exit 0 means a hand-edit is structurally valid.
- `board.py --background` reuses the running board or starts one, opens it,
  and prints its URL.
- Any error path prints `[error] <msg>` to stderr and exits 2, with no
  mutation to `portfolio.json`. Stop and surface the message verbatim.

## Verbs

### `idea <pitch>`
Run `add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<conversation context, ≤8 words>"`. The
source should summarize where the idea came from (e.g. "chat about GPS
vendor gaps"), not just "chat".

### `update <name> <note>`
Fuzzy-match `<name>` against the project names currently in the registry
(read `portfolio.json` first). If exactly one match, run `add-update "<name>"
"<note>"` (add `--next-action "<...>"` if the user gave one). If the match is
ambiguous or there's no close match, ask the user which project they mean
before running anything.

### `start` / `park` / `done <name>`
Fuzzy-match like `update`, then `set-status "<name>" active|paused|done`.
A start on a job/side/tool project needs a receiver within 7 days: if it has
none, ask who it is for and run `set-receiver` (never invent one).

### `rank`
Read `portfolio.json`, show the lane's active projects with their current
`rank` values, and ask for the new order. Never reorder ranks yourself —
only apply the order the user gives you. Rewrite the `rank` fields directly
with the Edit tool, then validate with `slate-check` (exit 0 = valid).
Dragging on the board does the same thing and is usually quicker.

### `promote <idea>`
Ask which lane (`job`, `side`, `system`, `knowledge`, `tool`) and for a
`next_action`. With the Edit tool: set the matching idea's `status` to
`promoted`, and append a new project entry to that lane at the next free
`rank` (max existing rank in that lane + 1). Validate with `slate-check`.

### `stage <name> <stage>`
Fuzzy-match `<name>` like `update` does. Run `set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"`.

**Shipped → harvest handoff:** when the stage being set is `shipped`, offer
once: "Want me to run /harvest on <name> to distill it into your SecondBrain
and log the shipped artifact?" On yes, invoke the `harvest` skill for that
project.

### bare `/project`
Run `board.py --background` and give the URL, then show `slate-check` output
in chat.

## After every mutation

Nothing to render: the board picks the change up on its next poll. Say what
changed in one line. Registry edits are committed by closeout as
`data: board edits <date>`; do not commit them mid-session unless asked.

## Rules

- Never reorder project ranks yourself — only apply the order the user
  gives you during `rank`.
- Never delete a project or idea without explicit confirmation.
- On any `[error] ...` output from the CLI: stop immediately and show the
  error verbatim.
- `portfolio.json` is the single source of truth; tasks live in each repo's
  `docs/STATUS.md`, which the board reads and never writes.
----
# Skill mechanics

The skill-specific branch of [`writing-for-agents`](SKILL.md): what changes when the document is a skill (frontmatter, the invocation choice, and router skills). Everything else about writing it is the universal reference in `SKILL.md`.

## Invocation

Two choices, trading the two loads:

- A **model-invoked** skill keeps a `description`, so the agent can fire it autonomously, and other skills can reach it. You can still type its name: model-invocation always _includes_ user reach; a description only ever adds agent discovery, never removes the human's. The description is the skill's top-level context pointer, forced to stay loaded at all times: permanent context load in exchange for discoverability. A model-invoked skill whose content is all reference is also one home for shared reference: another skill can invoke it, so reference needed by several skills lives in one place. Mechanics: omit `disable-model-invocation`, and write a model-facing description carrying the trigger branches (the pointer-writing rules in `SKILL.md` apply in full).
- A **user-invoked** skill strips the description from the agent's reach: only the human typing its name can invoke it, and no other skill can. Zero context load, but it spends cognitive load: you are the index that must remember it exists. Mechanics: set `disable-model-invocation: true`; the `description` becomes human-facing: a one-line summary, trigger lists stripped.

Pick model-invocation only when the agent must reach the skill on its own, or another skill must. If it only ever fires by hand, make it user-invoked and pay no context load.

Shared reference that two user-invoked skills both need can live in neither: with no descriptions, neither can fire the other. Push it to a plain file outside the skill system: external reference any skill can point at.

## Splitting by invocation

The invocation cut of splitting (the sequence cut lives in `SKILL.md`): split off a model-invoked skill when you have a distinct leading word that should trigger it on its own (a trigger word you actually use in your prompts), or another skill must reach it. You pay context load for the new always-loaded description, so that independent reach has to be worth it.

## Router skills

When user-invoked skills multiply past what you can remember, that piled-up cognitive load is cured by a **router skill**: one user-invoked skill that names the others and when to reach for each, so the human has one skill to remember instead of many. It can only hint, never fire them: user-invoked skills have no description, so nothing but the human can reach them.

"""Pure registry mutations behind the board. No HTTP, no file I/O."""
import datetime as _dt

import portfolio
from portfolio import RegistryError, STAGES, LANES, PROJECT_STATUSES

ARCHIVED = {"done", "dropped", "merged", "archived"}


def _now() -> str:
    """Curation timestamp, in the same shape portfolio.py's writers use."""
    return _dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")


def _guard_cap(data: dict, project: dict, lane: str, status: str) -> None:
    """Refuse to make a row an active job row when the slate is full (meta.slate.cap).

    The one start check for the board and the terminal (`portfolio.py set-status`), so
    the two cannot drift. A row that is already an active job row is not a start.
    """
    if lane != "job" or status != "active":
        return
    if project.get("lane") == "job" and project.get("status") == "active":
        return
    cap = ((data.get("meta") or {}).get("slate") or {}).get("cap")
    if not isinstance(cap, int):
        return
    active = [p["name"] for p in data.get("projects", [])
              if p.get("lane") == "job" and p.get("status") == "active" and p is not project]
    if len(active) >= cap:
        raise RegistryError(f"slate is full: {len(active)} of {cap} job projects active "
                            f"({', '.join(active)}). Park or finish one first.")


def find(data: dict, name: str) -> dict:
    for p in data["projects"]:
        if p["name"] == name:
            return p
    raise RegistryError(f"unknown project: {name}")


def live(data: dict, lane: str) -> list[dict]:
    return sorted(
        (p for p in data["projects"]
         if p.get("lane") == lane and p.get("status") not in ARCHIVED),
        key=lambda p: p.get("rank", 10**6),   # a missing rank sorts last; rank 0 is not "missing"
    )


def _renumber(data: dict, lane: str) -> None:
    members = live(data, lane)
    ordered: list[dict] = []
    for stage in STAGES:
        ordered.extend(p for p in members if p.get("stage") == stage)
    ordered.extend(p for p in members if p.get("stage") not in STAGES)
    for i, p in enumerate(ordered, 1):
        p["rank"] = i


def reorder(data: dict, name: str, lane: str, stage: str, position: int) -> dict:
    """Move a card. Deliberately does NOT stamp `curated_at`: a drag is a
    re-prioritisation, not a curation event, and stamping every drag would make a
    quiet paused row look recently worked: the Friday sweep (sweep.py) orders rows
    by `curated_at` among other dates. (render.py's stale signal, the original
    reason, retired 2026-10-03.) Do not "fix" this omission — see patch_project/
    promote, which do stamp.
    """
    if lane not in LANES:
        raise RegistryError(f"lane must be one of {sorted(LANES)}")
    if stage not in STAGES:
        raise RegistryError(f"stage must be one of {STAGES}")
    project = find(data, name)
    if project.get("status") in ARCHIVED:
        # fail with a message a user can act on, before touching anything
        raise RegistryError(f"{name}: cannot reorder an archived project")
    _guard_cap(data, project, lane, project.get("status"))
    old_lane = project.get("lane")

    project["lane"] = lane
    project["stage"] = stage

    # Rebuild the destination column with the card inserted at `position`,
    # then give every card in the column a rank that sorts it correctly.
    column = [p for p in live(data, lane) if p.get("stage") == stage and p is not project]
    column.insert(max(0, min(position, len(column))), project)
    for offset, p in enumerate(column):
        p["rank"] = -(len(column) - offset)   # temporary keys, fixed by _renumber

    _renumber(data, lane)
    if old_lane and old_lane != lane:
        _renumber(data, old_lane)
    return data


def promote(data, name, lane, stage, position, purpose, next_action):
    """Move an inbox record onto the board.

    Deliberately gate-free. This used to refuse a promotion without a purpose and
    a next action, which blocked the drag the board is built around — and the gate
    never held anyway: both fields could be cleared the moment after promotion and
    the registry still validated. A missing next action is now surfaced where it
    matters instead, as a flag on the board card, so the drag stays
    fast and the gap stays visible.
    """
    inbox = data.setdefault("inbox", [])
    record = next((r for r in inbox if r["name"] == name), None)
    if record is None:
        raise RegistryError(f"unknown inbox record: {name}")
    if any(p["name"] == name for p in data["projects"]):
        raise RegistryError(f"{name}: a project with this name already exists")
    _guard_cap(data, {}, lane, "active")          # a promoted row lands active

    project = {
        "name": record["name"],
        "dev_folder": record.get("dev_folder", record["name"]),
        "lane": lane,
        "rank": 10**6,                       # placeholder; reorder assigns the real one
        # Always active, never inherited. Most inbox records carry `paused` from
        # capture, and a promoted one landing paused was both a surprise and a
        # silent one — the needs-a-next-action flag is active-only, so the card
        # arrived unflagged too. Dragging onto the board means picking it up.
        # Pausing it again is one click on the pill.
        "status": "active",
        "stage": stage,
        # stripped so a whitespace-only field stores as "" and reads as blank to
        # the needs-a-next-action flag, rather than as a value that satisfies it
        "purpose": (purpose or "").strip(),
        "next_action": (next_action or "").strip(),
        "links": [],
        "updates": record.get("updates", []),
        "curated_at": _now(),                # promotion is a curation event
        "started": _dt.date.today().isoformat(),   # 7-day rule clock (seven_day.py)
    }
    data["projects"].append(project)
    try:
        reorder(data, name, lane, stage, position)
    except RegistryError:
        data["projects"].remove(project)     # leave the inbox untouched on failure
        raise
    data["inbox"] = [r for r in inbox if r["name"] != name]
    return data


def set_lane(data, name, lane):
    """Move a project between lanes, keeping its stage.

    The board only ever renders one lane and can only drop into the lane it is
    showing, so a mislabeled project could not be moved from the UI at all.

    Unlike a bare `reorder` this stamps `curated_at`: the distinction the rest of
    this module draws is drag = re-prioritisation (no stamp), edit = curation
    (stamp), and correcting a lane is a deliberate correction, not a drag.
    """
    if lane not in LANES:
        raise RegistryError(f"lane must be one of {sorted(LANES)}")
    project = find(data, name)
    old = project.get("lane")
    if old == lane:
        return data
    _guard_cap(data, project, lane, project.get("status"))

    stage = project.get("stage")
    if project.get("status") in ARCHIVED or stage not in STAGES:
        # `reorder` refuses archived projects, and rejects a project with no stage.
        # Move those by hand. An archived project was never in `live()`, so only the
        # lane it left needs renumbering; an unstaged one sorts after every staged
        # member in both lanes, which is where `_renumber` already puts it.
        project["lane"] = lane
        if project.get("status") not in ARCHIVED:
            _renumber(data, lane)
        if old:
            _renumber(data, old)
    else:
        reorder(data, name, lane, stage, 10**6)   # clamps to the end of the column
    project["curated_at"] = _now()
    return data


def _restore_to_inbox(data, project):
    """Put an inbox-retired idea back where it started, instead of leaving it a
    project with empty fields that bypasses the promotion gate."""
    lane = project.get("lane")
    record = {
        "name": project["name"],
        "dev_folder": project.get("dev_folder", project["name"]),
        "status": "active",
    }
    for field in ("purpose", "next_action"):        # carry back anything typed
        if (project.get(field) or "").strip():
            record[field] = project[field]
    if project.get("updates"):
        record["updates"] = project["updates"]
    data["projects"] = [p for p in data["projects"] if p is not project]
    data.setdefault("inbox", []).append(record)
    if lane:
        _renumber(data, lane)
    return data


def archive_inbox(data, name, lane, purpose="", next_action="", status="dropped"):
    """Retire an inbox idea straight to the Archive, no promotion gate.

    For ideas that never went anywhere: they skip purpose/next_action, which
    `promote` hard-requires. Deliberately does NOT call `reorder` — that raises on
    archived projects — so `rank` is set here instead. Any int >= 1 satisfies
    `portfolio.validate`, and the lane renumbering never reaches it because
    `live()` filters archived records out.
    """
    if status not in ARCHIVED:
        raise RegistryError(f"archive status must be one of {sorted(ARCHIVED)}")
    if lane not in LANES:
        raise RegistryError(f"lane must be one of {sorted(LANES)}")
    inbox = data.setdefault("inbox", [])
    record = next((r for r in inbox if r["name"] == name), None)
    if record is None:
        raise RegistryError(f"unknown inbox record: {name}")
    if any(p["name"] == name for p in data["projects"]):
        raise RegistryError(f"{name}: a project with this name already exists")

    data["projects"].append({
        "name": record["name"],
        "dev_folder": record.get("dev_folder", record["name"]),
        "lane": lane,
        "rank": 10**6,                       # never renumbered: live() skips archived
        "status": status,
        "stage": "idea",                     # where it died
        "purpose": (purpose or "").strip(),
        "next_action": (next_action or "").strip(),
        "links": [],
        "updates": record.get("updates", []),
        "curated_at": _now(),                # retiring an idea is a curation event
        # remembered so un-archiving can put it back in the inbox rather than
        # leaving a project with empty fields that skipped the promotion gate
        "archived_from_inbox": True,
    })
    data["inbox"] = [r for r in inbox if r["name"] != name]
    return data


def patch_project(data, name, *, status=None, purpose=None,
                  next_action=None, note=None, today=None, receiver=None):
    project = find(data, name)
    if receiver is not None:
        if not isinstance(receiver, str):
            raise RegistryError("receiver must be a string")
        if receiver.strip():
            project["receiver"] = receiver.strip()
        else:
            project.pop("receiver", None)     # blank clears it
    if status is not None:
        if status not in PROJECT_STATUSES:
            raise RegistryError(f"status must be one of {sorted(PROJECT_STATUSES)}")
        _guard_cap(data, project, project.get("lane"), status)
        was_archived = project.get("status") in ARCHIVED     # read before the write
        if status == "active" and project.get("status") != "active":
            # 7-day rule (seven_day.py): becoming active starts the clock, and a revived
            # row is a new start, so any grandfathering from 2026-10-03 is dropped.
            project["started"] = today or _dt.date.today().isoformat()
            project.pop("seven_day_exempt", None)
        project["status"] = status
        if was_archived and status not in ARCHIVED and project.pop("archived_from_inbox", False):
            # An inbox record may have been recreated under this name while the
            # project sat archived. Two records with one name would make
            # promote/delete_inbox act on the wrong one, so leave it a project.
            if not any(r["name"] == name for r in data.get("inbox", [])):
                return _restore_to_inbox(data, project)
    if purpose is not None:
        project["purpose"] = purpose
    if next_action is not None:
        project["next_action"] = next_action
    if note is not None and note.strip():
        project.setdefault("updates", []).insert(0, {"date": today, "note": note.strip()})
    project["curated_at"] = _now()            # editing a card is a curation event
    if project.get("lane"):
        _renumber(data, project["lane"])
    return data


def delete_project(data, name):
    project = find(data, name)
    lane = project.get("lane")
    data["projects"] = [p for p in data["projects"] if p is not project]
    if lane:
        _renumber(data, lane)
    return data


def delete_inbox(data, name):
    inbox = data.get("inbox", [])
    before = len(inbox)
    data["inbox"] = [r for r in inbox if r["name"] != name]
    if len(data["inbox"]) == before:
        raise RegistryError(f"unknown inbox record: {name}")
    return data

    if lane != "job" or status != "active":
        return
    if project.get("lane") == "job" and project.get("status") == "active":
        return
    cap = ((data.get("meta") or {}).get("slate") or {}).get("cap")
    if not isinstance(cap, int):
        return
    active = [p["name"] for p in data.get("projects", [])
              if p.get("lane") == "job" and p.get("status") == "active" and p is not project]
    if len(active) >= cap:
        raise RegistryError(f"slate is full: {len(active)} of {cap} job projects active "
                            f"({', '.join(active)}). Park or finish one first.")


def find(data: dict, name: str) -> dict:
    for p in data["projects"]:
        if p["name"] == name:
            return p
    raise RegistryError(f"unknown project: {name}")


def live(data: dict, lane: str) -> list[dict]:
    return sorted(
        (p for p in data["projects"]
         if p.get("lane") == lane and p.get("status") not in ARCHIVED),
        key=lambda p: p.get("rank", 10**6),   # a missing rank sorts last; rank 0 is not "missing"
    )


def _renumber(data: dict, lane: str) -> None:
    members = live(data, lane)
    ordered: list[dict] = []
    for stage in STAGES:
        ordered.extend(p for p in members if p.get("stage") == stage)
    ordered.extend(p for p in members if p.get("stage") not in STAGES)
    for i, p in enumerate(ordered, 1):
        p["rank"] = i


def reorder(data: dict, name: str, lane: str, stage: str, position: int) -> dict:
    """Move a card. Deliberately does NOT stamp `curated_at`: a drag is a
    re-prioritisation, not a curation event, and stamping every drag would make a
    quiet paused row look recently worked: the Friday sweep (sweep.py) orders rows
    by `curated_at` among other dates. (render.py's stale signal, the original
    reason, retired 2026-10-03.) Do not "fix" this omission — see patch_project/
    promote, which do stamp.
    """
    if lane not in LANES:
        raise RegistryError(f"lane must be one of {sorted(LANES)}")
    if stage not in STAGES:
        raise RegistryError(f"stage must be one of {STAGES}")
    project = find(data, name)
    if project.get("status") in ARCHIVED:
        # fail with a message a user can act on, before touching anything
        raise RegistryError(f"{name}: cannot reorder an archived project")
    _guard_cap(data, project, lane, project.get("status"))
    old_lane = project.get("lane")

    project["lane"] = lane
    project["stage"] = stage

    # Rebuild the destination column with the card inserted at `position`,
    # then give every card in the column a rank that sorts it correctly.
    column = [p for p in live(data, lane) if p.get("stage") == stage and p is not project]
    column.insert(max(0, min(position, len(column))), project)
    for offset, p in enumerate(column):
        p["rank"] = -(len(column) - offset)   # temporary keys, fixed by _renumber

    _renumber(data, lane)
    if old_lane and old_lane != lane:
        _renumber(data, old_lane)
    return data


def promote(data, name, lane, stage, position, purpose, next_action):
    """Move an inbox record onto the board.

    Deliberately gate-free. This used to refuse a promotion without a purpose and
    a next action, which blocked the drag the board is built around — and the gate
    never held anyway: both fields could be cleared the moment after promotion and
    the registry still validated. A missing next action is now surfaced where it
    matters instead, as a flag on the board card, so the drag stays
    fast and the gap stays visible.
    """
    inbox = data.setdefault("inbox", [])
    record = next((r for r in inbox if r["name"] == name), None)
    if record is None:
        raise RegistryError(f"unknown inbox record: {name}")
    if any(p["name"] == name for p in data["projects"]):
        raise RegistryError(f"{name}: a project with this name already exists")
    _guard_cap(data, {}, lane, "active")          # a promoted row lands active

    project = {
        "name": record["name"],
        "dev_folder": record.get("dev_folder", record["name"]),
        "lane": lane,
        "rank": 10**6,                       # placeholder; reorder assigns the real one
        # Always active, never inherited. Most inbox records carry `paused` from
        # capture, and a promoted one landing paused was both a surprise and a
        # silent one — the needs-a-next-action flag is active-only, so the card
        # arrived unflagged too. Dragging onto the board means picking it up.
        # Pausing it again is one click on the pill.
        "status": "active",
        "stage": stage,
        # stripped so a whitespace-only field stores as "" and reads as blank to
        # the needs-a-next-action flag, rather than as a value that satisfies it
        "purpose": (purpose or "").strip(),
        "next_action": (next_action or "").strip(),
        "links": [],
        "updates": record.get("updates", []),
        "curated_at": _now(),                # promotion is a curation event
        "started": _dt.date.today().isoformat(),   # 7-day rule clock (seven_day.py)
    }
    data["projects"].append(project)
    try:
        reorder(data, name, lane, stage, position)
    except RegistryError:
        data["projects"].remove(project)     # leave the inbox untouched on failure
        raise
    data["inbox"] = [r for r in inbox if r["name"] != name]
    return data


def set_lane(data, name, lane):
    """Move a project between lanes, keeping its stage.

    The board only ever renders one lane and can only drop into the lane it is
    showing, so a mislabeled project could not be moved from the UI at all.

    Unlike a bare `reorder` this stamps `curated_at`: the distinction the rest of
    this module draws is drag = re-prioritisation (no stamp), edit = curation
    (stamp), and correcting a lane is a deliberate correction, not a drag.
    """
    if lane not in LANES:
        raise RegistryError(f"lane must be one of {sorted(LANES)}")
    project = find(data, name)
    old = project.get("lane")
    if old == lane:
        return data
    _guard_cap(data, project, lane, project.get("status"))

    stage = project.get("stage")
    if project.get("status") in ARCHIVED or stage not in STAGES:
        # `reorder` refuses archived projects, and rejects a project with no stage.
        # Move those by hand. An archived project was never in `live()`, so only the
        # lane it left needs renumbering; an unstaged one sorts after every staged
        # member in both lanes, which is where `_renumber` already puts it.
        project["lane"] = lane
        if project.get("status") not in ARCHIVED:
            _renumber(data, lane)
        if old:
            _renumber(data, old)
    else:
        reorder(data, name, lane, stage, 10**6)   # clamps to the end of the column
    project["curated_at"] = _now()
    return data


def _restore_to_inbox(data, project):
    """Put an inbox-retired idea back where it started, instead of leaving it a
    project with empty fields that bypasses the promotion gate."""
    lane = project.get("lane")
    record = {
        "name": project["name"],
        "dev_folder": project.get("dev_folder", project["name"]),
        "status": "active",
    }
    for field in ("purpose", "next_action"):        # carry back anything typed
        if (project.get(field) or "").strip():
            record[field] = project[field]
    if project.get("updates"):
        record["updates"] = project["updates"]
    data["projects"] = [p for p in data["projects"] if p is not project]
    data.setdefault("inbox", []).append(record)
    if lane:
        _renumber(data, lane)
    return data


def archive_inbox(data, name, lane, purpose="", next_action="", status="dropped"):
    """Retire an inbox idea straight to the Archive, no promotion gate.

    For ideas that never went anywhere: they skip purpose/next_action, which
    `promote` hard-requires. Deliberately does NOT call `reorder` — that raises on
    archived projects — so `rank` is set here instead. Any int >= 1 satisfies
    `portfolio.validate`, and the lane renumbering never reaches it because
    `live()` filters archived records out.
    """
    if status not in ARCHIVED:
        raise RegistryError(f"archive status must be one of {sorted(ARCHIVED)}")
    if lane not in LANES:
        raise RegistryError(f"lane must be one of {sorted(LANES)}")
    inbox = data.setdefault("inbox", [])
    record = next((r for r in inbox if r["name"] == name), None)
    if record is None:
        raise RegistryError(f"unknown inbox record: {name}")
    if any(p["name"] == name for p in data["projects"]):
        raise RegistryError(f"{name}: a project with this name already exists")

    data["projects"].append({
        "name": record["name"],
        "dev_folder": record.get("dev_folder", record["name"]),
        "lane": lane,
        "rank": 10**6,                       # never renumbered: live() skips archived
        "status": status,
        "stage": "idea",                     # where it died
        "purpose": (purpose or "").strip(),
        "next_action": (next_action or "").strip(),
        "links": [],
        "updates": record.get("updates", []),
        "curated_at": _now(),                # retiring an idea is a curation event
        # remembered so un-archiving can put it back in the inbox rather than
        # leaving a project with empty fields that skipped the promotion gate
        "archived_from_inbox": True,
    })
    data["inbox"] = [r for r in inbox if r["name"] != name]
    return data


def patch_project(data, name, *, status=None, purpose=None,
                  next_action=None, note=None, today=None, receiver=None):
    project = find(data, name)
    if receiver is not None:
        if not isinstance(receiver, str):
            raise RegistryError("receiver must be a string")
        if receiver.strip():
            project["receiver"] = receiver.strip()
        else:
            project.pop("receiver", None)     # blank clears it
    if status is not None:
        if status not in PROJECT_STATUSES:
            raise RegistryError(f"status must be one of {sorted(PROJECT_STATUSES)}")
        _guard_cap(data, project, project.get("lane"), status)
        was_archived = project.get("status") in ARCHIVED     # read before the write
        if status == "active" and project.get("status") != "active":
            # 7-day rule (seven_day.py): becoming active starts the clock, and a revived
            # row is a new start, so any grandfathering from 2026-10-03 is dropped.
            project["started"] = today or _dt.date.today().isoformat()
            project.pop("seven_day_exempt", None)
        project["status"] = status
        if was_archived and status not in ARCHIVED and project.pop("archived_from_inbox", False):
            # An inbox record may have been recreated under this name while the
            # project sat archived. Two records with one name would make
            # promote/delete_inbox act on the wrong one, so leave it a project.
            if not any(r["name"] == name for r in data.get("inbox", [])):
                return _restore_to_inbox(data, project)
    if purpose is not None:
        project["purpose"] = purpose
    if next_action is not None:
        project["next_action"] = next_action
    if note is not None and note.strip():
        project.setdefault("updates", []).insert(0, {"date": today, "note": note.strip()})
    project["curated_at"] = _now()            # editing a card is a curation event
    if project.get("lane"):
        _renumber(data, project["lane"])
    return data


def delete_project(data, name):
    project = find(data, name)
    lane = project.get("lane")
    data["projects"] = [p for p in data["projects"] if p is not project]
    if lane:
        _renumber(data, lane)
    return data


def delete_inbox(data, name):
    inbox = data.get("inbox", [])
    before = len(inbox)
    data["inbox"] = [r for r in inbox if r["name"] != name]
    if len(data["inbox"]) == before:
        raise RegistryError(f"unknown inbox record: {name}")
    return data

- `portfolio.py` run as a script is `__main__`, so modules it imports raise a different `RegistryError` class; new CLI branches catch `<module>.RegistryError` by name (see `set-status`, `sweep-decide`).
- Playwright sync API only processes page events inside Playwright calls: use `page.wait_for_timeout`, never `time.sleep`, in browser checks.
- The board's "unpushed edits" nudge refreshes on the next registry change, not on a `git push`.
- Regenerate calendar blocks ~2026-09-28. Handoff: `docs/handoffs/2026-09-14-prioritization-system.md`.
- `portfolio.py` must stay importable on its own: tests copy it alone into scratch dirs, so `slate` is imported lazily inside `slate-check` only.
- Registry changes get their own `data:` commit.

---
name: project
description: >-
  Manage the portfolio project registry (ideas, progress notes, ranking, promotion, dev stages,
  start/park/done, receivers) and open the live project board. Use when the user says
  "/project", "new idea:", "add to my project inbox", "log progress on", "show my projects",
  "re-rank my projects", "promote <idea>", "set the stage on" / "mark <project> as
  spec'd/planned/shipped", "start/park <project>". Do not use for the DEV drift dashboard
  (use project-triage) or to scaffold a new repo (use new-project).
---

# /project: portfolio registry

Drives the `project-triage` CLI. The registry, `portfolio.json`, is the single
source of truth; each repo's `docs/STATUS.md` holds its tasks, which the board
reads and never writes.

## Paths

- `$PT` is the folder holding `portfolio_json` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`
  (`config.macos.json` on the Mac: `~/DEV/project-triage`).
- Interpreter: `python3` on the Mac (there is no `python`); `python` on Windows.
- `portfolio.py` makes every change and always writes the live `$PT/portfolio.json` (only
  `slate-check` and the read commands take `--registry`). `board.py` serves the board.

## CLI

```
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<source>"
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" add-update "<name>" "<note>" [--next-action "<step>"]
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-status "<name>" active|paused|done [--note "<note>"]
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-receiver "<name>" "<who, or me: why>"
python3 "$PT/board.py" --background
```

| Command | Prints on success |
|---|---|
| `add-idea` | `idea captured (<N> in inbox)` |
| `add-update` | `updated <name>` |
| `set-stage` | `stage set: <name> → <stage>` |
| `set-status` | `status set: <name> → <status>` |
| `set-receiver` | `<Name>: receiver <who>` |
| `board.py --background` | `board started at <url>` or `board already running at <url>` |

- Names match case-insensitively. Stages, in ladder order: `idea grilled spec planned building shipped`.
- `set-status active` on a row that was not active stamps `started` and renumbers the lane.
- Every `portfolio.py` error prints `[error] <msg>` to stderr, exits 2 and leaves
  `portfolio.json` unchanged. `board.py` prints `board did not start; see <log>` and exits 1.
  Either way: stop and show the message verbatim.

## Ideas live off the board

`add-idea` appends to the registry's `ideas` list. The board shows projects and its own
`inbox` list, never `ideas`. So after capturing an idea, say it is in the ideas list
(N waiting) and that `/project promote <idea>` puts it on the board.

## Verbs

**Name matching** (every verb that takes `<name>`): read `portfolio.json` and match the name
against `projects[].name`. One clear match: use that exact name. Several or none: ask Eric
which project before running anything.

### `idea <pitch>`
`add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<where it came from, ≤8 words>"`, e.g. `--source "chat about
GPS vendor gaps"` (a place, not just "chat").

### `update <name> <note>`
`add-update "<name>" "<note>"`, plus `--next-action "<step>"` when Eric gave one.

### `start` / `park` / `done <name>`
`set-status "<name>" active|paused|done`, with `--note` when Eric gave a reason. Starting a
`job`, `side` or `tool` row with no `receiver`: ask Eric who it is for, then run
`set-receiver` with his words (`me: <why>` when it is for himself).

### `stage <name> <stage>`
`set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"`. When the stage is `shipped`, offer once: "Want me to run
/harvest on <name> to distill it into your SecondBrain and log the shipped artifact?" On
yes, invoke the `harvest` skill for that project.

### `promote <idea>` and `rank`
Both change the registry where no CLI command reaches. Follow
[`REGISTRY-EDITS.md`](REGISTRY-EDITS.md). Ranks come only from Eric: show the lane, ask
for his order, apply exactly that. Dragging cards on the board re-ranks faster.

### bare `/project`
Run `board.py --background` and give the URL. Then list the `ideas` with
`status: inbox` (first ~80 characters of each pitch), since the board does not show them.

## After a change

The board picks up registry changes on its next poll (a few seconds); there is nothing to
render. Tell Eric in one line what changed. Closeout commits the registry as
`data: board edits <date>`, so leave `portfolio.json` uncommitted unless Eric asks.

Delete a project or idea only after Eric confirms that exact row.

**Done when:** the command printed its success line (or the hand edit saved and the
`.bak` beside `portfolio.json` was refreshed), and Eric has the one-line summary.

# /project — portfolio registry skill

Drives the `project-triage` CLI to capture ideas, log progress and change
project status. The registry (`portfolio.json`) is the single source of truth.
The live board (`board.py`) is its front door and re-renders on its own within
a few seconds of any registry change, so there is nothing to render or publish.
(The static `dashboard.html`, its Artifact and `pulse.md` retired 2026-10-03.)

## Paths

- Config: `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.windows.json` on Windows; `config.macos.json` on macOS
- Repo: parent directory of `portfolio_json` in the selected platform config
- Interpreter: `python` on Windows; `python3` on macOS
- Registry: `portfolio_json` in the selected platform config
- CLI entry points: `portfolio.py` (mutations and checks), `board.py` (the board)

## CLI contract (verbatim — do not alter flags)

```
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<source>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" add-update "<name>" "<note>" --next-action "<optional>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" set-status "<name>" active|paused|done --note "<optional>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" set-receiver "<name>" "<who, or me: why>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" slate-check
python "<project-triage-repo>/board.py" --background
```

- `add-idea` prints `idea captured (<N> in inbox)`.
- `add-update` prints `updated <name>` (name match is case-insensitive).
- `set-stage` prints `stage set: <name> → <stage>`. Valid stages, in ladder
  order: `idea grilled spec planned building shipped`.

  the 7-day clock.

  rules; exit 0 means a hand-edit is structurally valid.

`promote` and `rank` change `portfolio.json` through `portfolio.load_registry` /
`save_registry`, run from `$PT` (see SKILL.md, Paths). Use these functions, not the Edit
tool: `save_registry` validates the whole file first, refreshes `portfolio.json.bak`
(the proof of who wrote the file, which the provenance rule relies on), and replaces the
file atomically while the board polls it.

A refused save raises `RegistryError: <problems>` and leaves the file unchanged: show it
verbatim and stop.

## promote `<idea>`

1. Find the idea: `ideas[]` rows with `status: inbox` whose `pitch` matches. One match, or
   ask Eric which.
2. Check `projects[]` for a row that already carries this idea (another session may have
   added it). If one exists, only set the idea's `status` to `promoted` and say so.
3. Ask Eric for the lane (`job`, `side`, `system`, `knowledge`, `tool`), the project name
   (`Words_With_Underscores`, matching the DEV folder when there is one), and the next
   action. Take `purpose` as one line from the pitch.
4. Save the row as paused, then start it with the CLI, which stamps `started` and gives
   the row its rank in the lane:

```
cd "$PT" && python3 - <<'EOF'
import datetime as dt
from pathlib import Path
import portfolio as pf
p = Path("portfolio.json"); d = pf.load_registry(p)
idea = [i for i in d["ideas"] if i["status"] == "inbox" and "<words from the pitch>" in i["pitch"]]
assert len(idea) == 1, [i["pitch"][:60] for i in idea]
name = "<Project_Name>"
assert not any(x["name"].lower() == name.lower() for x in d["projects"]), f"{name} exists"
idea[0]["status"] = "promoted"
d["projects"].append({
    "name": name, "dev_folder": "<DEV folder, or the name>", "lane": "<lane>",
    "rank": 10**6, "status": "paused", "stage": "idea",
    "purpose": "<one line>", "next_action": "<next action>",
    "links": [], "updates": [], "source": f"idea {idea[0]['captured_at'][:10]}",
    "curated_at": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
})
pf.save_registry(p, d)
print("saved", name)
EOF
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-status "<Project_Name>" active --note "promoted from the ideas list"
```

5. A `job`, `side` or `tool` row also gets a receiver: the start step in SKILL.md.

The board orders each lane by stage first (`idea` → `shipped`, unstaged rows last), then by
`rank` within a stage, and every board edit renumbers the lane that way. So a rank order
holds only within a stage.

1. Show the lane's active rows grouped by stage, in current `rank` order, and ask Eric for
   his order. If his order crosses stages, tell him the stage grouping wins.
2. Apply exactly his order: his rows take temporary ranks below 1 in that order, and the
   board's own renumbering turns them into ranks 1..n:

```
cd "$PT" && python3 - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
import portfolio as pf, board_ops
p = Path("portfolio.json"); d = pf.load_registry(p)
lane, order = "<lane>", ["<Name1>", "<Name2>"]   # Eric's order
for i, name in enumerate(order):
    row = board_ops.find(d, name); assert row["lane"] == lane, name
    row["rank"] = i - len(order)                  # temporary; renumbered next line

pf.save_registry(p, d)
print([(x["name"], x["rank"], x.get("stage")) for x in board_ops.live(d, lane) if x["status"] == "active"])
EOF
```

3. Show Eric the printed order.

`save_registry`, run from `$PT` (see SKILL.md, Paths). Use these functions, not the Edit

(the proof of who wrote the file, which the provenance rule relies on), and replaces the
file atomically while the board polls it.

A refused save raises `RegistryError: <problems>` and leaves the file unchanged: show it
verbatim and stop.

## promote `<idea>`

1. Find the idea: `ideas[]` rows with `status: inbox` whose `pitch` matches. One match, or
   ask Eric which.
2. Check `projects[]` for a row that already carries this idea (another session may have
   added it). If one exists, only set the idea's `status` to `promoted` and say so.

   (`Words_With_Underscores`, matching the DEV folder when there is one), and the next
   action. Take `purpose` as one line from the pitch.
4. Save the row as paused, then start it with the CLI, which stamps `started` and gives
   the row its rank in the lane:

```
cd "$PT" && python3 - <<'EOF'
import datetime as dt
from pathlib import Path

## Paths

- `$PT` is the folder holding `portfolio_json` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`
  (`config.macos.json` on the Mac: `~/DEV/project-triage`).
- Interpreter: `python3` on the Mac (there is no `python`); `python` on Windows.
- `portfolio.py` makes every change and always writes the live `$PT/portfolio.json` (only
  `slate-check` and the read commands take `--registry`). `board.py` serves the board.

## CLI

```
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<source>"
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" add-update "<name>" "<note>" [--next-action "<step>"]
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-status "<name>" active|paused|done [--note "<note>"]
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-receiver "<name>" "<who, or me: why>"
python3 "$PT/board.py" --background
```

| Command | Prints on success |
|---|---|
| `add-idea` | `idea captured (<N> in inbox)` |
| `add-update` | `updated <name>` |
| `set-stage` | `stage set: <name> → <stage>` |
| `set-status` | `status set: <name> → <status>` |
| `set-receiver` | `<Name>: receiver <who>` |
| `board.py --background` | `board started at <url>` or `board already running at <url>` |

- Names match case-insensitively. Stages, in ladder order: `idea grilled spec planned building shipped`.
- `set-status active` on a row that was not active stamps `started` and renumbers the lane.
- Every `portfolio.py` error prints `[error] <msg>` to stderr, exits 2 and leaves
  `portfolio.json` unchanged. `board.py` prints `board did not start; see <log>` and exits 1.
  Either way: stop and show the message verbatim.

## Ideas live off the board

---
name: project
description: >-
  Manage the portfolio project registry (ideas, progress notes, ranking, promotion, dev stages,
  start/park/done, receivers) and open the live project board. Use when the user says
  "/project", "new idea:", "log progress on", "show my projects", "re-rank my projects",
  "promote <idea>", "mark <project> as spec'd/planned/shipped", "start/park <project>". Do not use for the DEV drift dashboard
  (use project-triage) or to scaffold a new repo (use new-project).
---

# /project: portfolio registry

Drives the `project-triage` CLI. The registry, `portfolio.json`, is the single
source of truth; each repo's `docs/STATUS.md` holds its tasks, which the board
reads only.

## Paths

- `$PT` is the folder holding `portfolio_json` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`
  (`config.macos.json` on the Mac: `~/DEV/project-triage`).
- Interpreter: `python3` on the Mac (there is no `python`); `python` on Windows.
- `portfolio.py` makes every change and always writes the live `$PT/portfolio.json` (only
  `slate-check` and the read commands take `--registry`). `board.py` serves the board.

## CLI

```
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<source>"
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" add-update "<name>" "<note>" [--next-action "<step>"]
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-status "<name>" active|paused|done [--note "<note>"]
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-receiver "<name>" "<who, or me: why>"
python3 "$PT/board.py" --background
```

| Command | Prints on success |
|---|---|
| `add-idea` | `idea captured (<N> in inbox)` |
| `add-update` | `updated <name>` |
| `set-stage` | `stage set: <name> → <stage>` |
| `set-status` | `status set: <name> → <status>` |
| `set-receiver` | `<Name>: receiver <who>` |
| `board.py --background` | `board started at <url>` or `board already running at <url>` |

- Names match case-insensitively. Stages, in ladder order: `idea grilled spec planned building shipped`.
- `set-status active` on a row that was not active stamps `started` and renumbers the lane.
- Every `portfolio.py` error prints `[error] <msg>` to stderr, exits 2 and leaves
  `portfolio.json` unchanged. `board.py` prints `board did not start; see <log>` and exits 1.
  Either way: stop and show the message verbatim.

## Ideas live off the board

`add-idea` appends to the registry's `ideas` list. The board shows projects and its own
`inbox` list; `ideas` appear only in chat. So after capturing an idea, say it is in the
ideas list (N waiting) and that `/project promote <idea>` puts it on the board.

## Verbs

**Name matching** (every verb that takes `<name>`): read `portfolio.json` and match the name
against `projects[].name`. One clear match: use that exact name. Several or none: ask Eric
which project before running anything.

### `idea <pitch>`
`add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<where it came from, ≤8 words>"`, e.g. `--source "chat about
GPS vendor gaps"` (a place, not just "chat").

### `update <name> <note>`
`add-update "<name>" "<note>"`, plus `--next-action "<step>"` when Eric gave one.

### `start` / `park` / `done <name>`
`set-status "<name>" active|paused|done`, with `--note` when Eric gave a reason. Starting a
`job`, `side` or `tool` row with no `receiver`: ask Eric who it is for, then run
`set-receiver` with his words (`me: <why>` when it is for himself).

### `stage <name> <stage>`
`set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"`. When the stage is `shipped`, offer once: "Want me to run
/harvest on <name> to distill it into your SecondBrain and log the shipped artifact?" On
yes, invoke the `harvest` skill for that project.

### `promote <idea>` and `rank`
Both change the registry where no CLI command reaches: follow
[`REGISTRY-EDITS.md`](REGISTRY-EDITS.md). Dragging cards on the board re-ranks faster.

### bare `/project`
Run `board.py --background` and give the URL. Then list the `ideas` with
`status: inbox` (first ~80 characters of each pitch), since the board does not show them.

## After a change

The board picks up registry changes on its next poll (a few seconds); there is nothing to
render. Tell Eric in one line what changed. Closeout commits the registry as
`data: board edits <date>`, so leave `portfolio.json` uncommitted unless Eric asks.

Delete a project or idea only after Eric confirms that exact row.

**Done when:** the command printed its success line (or the hand edit saved and the
`.bak` beside `portfolio.json` was refreshed), and Eric has the one-line summary.

# /project: portfolio registry

Drives the `project-triage` CLI. The registry, `portfolio.json`, is the single
source of truth; each repo's `docs/STATUS.md` holds its tasks, which the board
reads only.

## Paths

- `$PT` is the folder holding `portfolio_json` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`.
  On the Mac that is `~/DEV/project-triage`: start each Bash call with
  `PT=~/DEV/project-triage` (the shell does not keep it between calls).
- Interpreter: `python3` on the Mac (there is no `python`). On Windows, use `python` and the
  `portfolio_json` folder from `config.windows.json` wherever this skill says `python3` and `$PT`.

  `slate-check` and the read commands take `--registry`). `board.py` serves the board.

python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-status "<name>" active|paused|done [--note "<note>"]
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-receiver "<name>" "<who, or me: why>"

# /project: portfolio registry

Drives the `project-triage` CLI. The registry, `portfolio.json`, is the single
source of truth; each repo's `docs/STATUS.md` holds its tasks, which the board
reads only.

## Paths

- `$PT` is the folder holding `portfolio_json` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`.
  On the Mac that is `~/DEV/project-triage`: start each Bash call with
  `PT=~/DEV/project-triage` (the shell does not keep it between calls).
- Interpreter: `python3` on the Mac (there is no `python`). On Windows, use `python` and the
  `portfolio_json` folder from `config.windows.json` wherever this skill says `python3` and `$PT`.
- `portfolio.py` makes every change and always writes the live `$PT/portfolio.json` (only
  `slate-check` and the read commands take `--registry`). `board.py` serves the board.

## CLI

```
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<source>"
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" add-update "<name>" "<note>" [--next-action "<step>"]
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-status "<name>" active|paused|done [--note "<note>"]
python3 "$PT/portfolio.py" set-receiver "<name>" "<who, or me: why>"
python3 "$PT/board.py" --background
```

| Command | Prints on success |

ideas list (N waiting) and that `/project promote <idea>` puts it on the board.

## Verbs

**Name matching** (every verb that takes `<name>`): read `portfolio.json` and match the name
against `projects[].name`. One clear match: use that exact name. Several or none: ask Eric
which project before running anything.

### `idea <pitch>`
`add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<where it came from, ≤8 words>"`, e.g. `--source "chat about
GPS vendor gaps"` (a place, not just "chat").

### `update <name> <note>`
`add-update "<name>" "<note>"`, plus `--next-action "<step>"` when Eric gave one.

### `start` / `park` / `done <name>`
`set-status "<name>" active|paused|done`, with `--note` when Eric gave a reason. Starting a
`job`, `side` or `tool` row with no `receiver`: ask Eric who it is for, then run
`set-receiver` with his words (`me: <why>` when it is for himself).

### `stage <name> <stage>`
`set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"`. When the stage is `shipped`, offer once: "Want me to run
/harvest on <name> to distill it into your SecondBrain and log the shipped artifact?" On
yes, invoke the `harvest` skill for that project.

Both change the registry where no CLI command reaches: follow
[`REGISTRY-EDITS.md`](REGISTRY-EDITS.md). Dragging cards on the board re-ranks faster.

`status: inbox` (first ~80 characters of each pitch), since the board does not show them.

The board picks up registry changes on its next poll (a few seconds); there is nothing to
render. Tell Eric in one line what changed. Closeout commits the registry as
`data: board edits <date>`, so leave `portfolio.json` uncommitted unless Eric asks.

Delete a project or idea only after Eric confirms that exact row.

**Done when:** the command printed its success line (or the hand edit saved and the
`.bak` beside `portfolio.json` was refreshed), and Eric has the one-line summary.
